identity.title: RG-SAN: Rule-Guided Spatial Awareness Network for End-to-End 3D Referring Expression Segmentation

problem.claim: 3D referring expression segmentation correlates referring expressions with point clouds to segment described 3D objects.

gap.claim: Traditional approaches often over-segment or mis-segment because they insufficiently emphasize instance spatial information.

contributions.claim: Introduces RG-SAN, using only target-instance spatial information for supervision, with a text-driven localization module and a rule-guided weak-supervision strategy.
The TLM locates and iteratively refines mentioned instances, while dependency-tree rules guide positioning of the core instance when only the target has supervised positional information.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper presents a rule-guided spatial-awareness network that combines iterative localization with dependency-tree-guided weak supervision based solely on target-instance spatial information.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive ScanRefer testing and a 5.1-point mIoU increase, establishing new performance benchmarks.
The authors report significant robustness improvements on descriptions containing spatial ambiguity.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines 3D referring expression segmentation as linking language descriptions to point clouds for object segmentation.
Attributes common over-segmentation and mis-segmentation to insufficient attention to instance spatial information.
Introduces RG-SAN, comprising TLM for iterative localization and RWS for dependency-tree-guided positioning under target-only supervision.
Reports a 5.1-point mIoU gain and improved robustness to spatial ambiguity on ScanRefer.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns a supervision limitation—only target objects have positional labels—with a dependency-tree rule strategy designed to guide the core instance.

lessons.interpretation: Making the supervision constraint explicit can motivate a targeted mechanism rather than leaving weak supervision underspecified.
lessons.application: State the available labels and map each missing supervision signal to a concrete rule, module, or training constraint.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when dense annotations are available or when dependency-tree structure does not represent the task reliably.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the ScanRefer baselines, evaluation protocol, absolute mIoU values, or statistical details behind the reported improvements.
It does not provide ablations separating the TLM and RWS contributions or details of the robustness evaluation.
